cues.en: Let's talk cost and how much it will cost you to follow along in this course, but also cost in general.
cues.zh: 來談談費用，包括跟著這門課練習會花多少錢，以及一般 AI 使用費用。

cues.en: The topic is really, really difficult to place in a course like this because it could either be at the front, but then we'll
cues.zh: 這個主題很難安排在這類課程的哪個位置。放在最前面，

cues.en: talk, in this case, I will talk about some concepts that haven't been explained yet, or it can be at the end, which I think is too late, so I'll put it
cues.zh: 就得提到一些還沒解釋的概念；放在最後面，我又覺得太晚，所以我決定

cues.en: up front.
cues.zh: 先在前面介紹。

cues.en: Bear with me that there is a few things we haven't talked about yet in this,
cues.zh: 這段會提到一些我們還沒講過的內容，請先包涵。

cues.en: and they will be, of course, explained along the way, and I will give some high levels in this video.
cues.zh: 之後都會逐一解釋，這段影片先從較高層次概覽。

cues.en: The good thing about cost when it comes to AI in general is that it's a pay-for-what-you-use approach in all of the providers.
cues.zh: 一般而言，AI 費用有個好處：各家供應商都是依實際使用量收費。

cues.en: So there's no idle fees, meaning that if I make an Azure account or an OpenAI account and don't use it for a month, it's not like it costs you anything compared
cues.zh: 沒有閒置費用。也就是說，建立 Azure 或 OpenAI 帳號後，整個月都不用，不會因此產生費用，這和

cues.en: to, for example, if you had an Azure app service.
cues.zh: Azure App Service 等服務不同。

cues.en: If you use it or not, you would pay because it's a spinning system.
cues.zh: 那類服務持續在運作，不管有沒有使用，都需要付費。

cues.en: So it won't cost you anything to have multiple accounts to different providers.
cues.zh: 因此，同時擁有多家供應商的帳號，本身不會產生費用。

cues.en: I have, like, 10 different, and it doesn't cost me anything when I don't use them.
cues.zh: 我大概有十家的帳號，不使用時都不會付錢。

cues.en: There's, however, that most providers need to charge up your account with, like, around $5.
cues.zh: 不過，大部分供應商會要求先替帳號儲值，大約 5 美元。

cues.en: Azure and Google being the exception, where you can pay as you go, and then you pay after the fact.
cues.zh: Azure 和 Google 是例外，可以隨用隨付，使用後才計費。

cues.en: But if you want an OpenAI account, you need to spend up front $5, and then you can, of course, use those as you
cues.zh: 如果使用 OpenAI，就得先儲值 5 美元，再隨著

cues.en: go along.
cues.zh: 使用逐步扣款。

cues.en: And $5 would be plenty to follow this course.
cues.zh: 5 美元已經很夠跟著這門課練習。

cues.en: There are a few providers that offer free tiers with some heavy rate limits.
cues.zh: 有些供應商提供免費額度，但速率限制比較嚴格。

cues.en: Google have some free tier.
cues.zh: Google 有免費方案，

cues.en: GitHub models have a free tier.
cues.zh: GitHub Models 也有，

cues.en: Hugging Face and Cohere have as well.
cues.zh: Hugging Face 和 Cohere 同樣有免費方案。

cues.en: But, for example, Cohere, you can make one call per minute.
cues.zh: 例如 Cohere，可能每分鐘只能呼叫一次。

cues.en: And Google, you can only use all the very, very cheap models, not some of the more advanced models and so on.
cues.zh: Google 的免費方案則只能使用比較便宜的模型，無法使用某些進階模型等等。

cues.en: What you pay is not in amount of time you spend on the LLM or anything.
cues.zh: 費用不是依照你使用 LLM 的時間來計算。

cues.en: You pay in what is called tokens.
cues.zh: 而是依照所謂的 Token 計費。

cues.en: Let's learn what those are.
cues.zh: 來看看 Token 是什麼。

cues.en: Tokens is a kind of language translation from
cues.zh: Token 可以想成一種語言轉換，

cues.en: English to a language of tokens, which is common words set together in order to not
cues.zh: 把英文轉成 Token 的語言，將常見文字組合成單位，如此就不需要

cues.en: need to know every single word in the English language.
cues.zh: 為英文裡的每一個完整單字各自建立表示。

cues.en: So you can see here I have made a high.
cues.zh: 例如這裡我輸入了一段文字，開頭是 Hi。

cues.en: This is a sample on how many tokens there are in this sentence.
cues.zh: 這個範例顯示，這段句子會拆成多少 Token。

cues.en: And you can see "-this", "-is", "-a", is a token by themselves.
cues.zh: 可以看到 this、is、a，這些單字各自就是一個 Token。

cues.en: So I use very, very common words here.
cues.zh: 因為這裡使用的都是很常見的字。

cues.en: But have I used an uncommon word like platypus?
cues.zh: 如果改用比較少見的單字，例如 platypus，也就是鴨嘴獸，

cues.en: That would have been broken up into multiple tokens because it won't have a specific token by itself.
cues.zh: 就可能拆成多個 Token，因為不一定有一個專屬的 Token 表示它。

cues.en: But I have one token specifically set to it.
cues.zh: 常見的字則可能各有自己的 Token。

cues.en: So these 66 characters is 15 tokens in total.
cues.zh: 所以這 66 個字元，總共是 15 個 Token。

cues.en: And you roughly learn that you shouldn't really care about this too much.
cues.zh: 大致理解後，其實不必對這件事太過糾結。

cues.en: You know many tokens, less tokens and so on.
cues.zh: 知道 Token 多或少的概念即可。

cues.en: 15 tokens is not a lot.
cues.zh: 15 個 Token 並不多。

cues.en: You pay in three different or four different ways.
cues.zh: 計費可以分成三種，或細分成四種。

cues.en: You pay for input tokens.
cues.zh: 首先是輸入 Token，

cues.en: That is your prompt.
cues.zh: 也就是你的提示詞。

cues.en: So if we say, what is the capital of France?
cues.zh: 例如問「法國的首都是哪裡？」，

cues.en: We pay for the tokens of that sentence.
cues.zh: 就要支付這句話的 Token 費用。

cues.en: There will be additional input tokens that you also pay for.
cues.zh: 此外還可能有其他需要付費的輸入 Token。

cues.en: Like whenever we introduce tools and structured output and stuff, there will be additional metadata that need to be sent to the LLM.
cues.zh: 例如之後介紹工具和結構化輸出時，還必須把額外的中繼資料送給 LLM。

cues.en: For example, when we say, what is the weather in Paris?
cues.zh: 假設我們問「巴黎的天氣如何？」，

cues.en: And we have a weather tool.
cues.zh: 而且有一個天氣工具，

cues.en: We will also pay for the schema that says, how is that tool defined?
cues.zh: 那麼描述工具如何定義的結構描述，也會算入費用。

cues.en: So even if you say, hi, and you have a lot of tools, it will cost you more tokens.
cues.zh: 所以就算只說 Hi，如果附帶很多工具，仍會消耗更多 Token。

cues.en: We will get into that when we talk tools.
cues.zh: 工具章節會再深入介紹。

cues.en: Then there's something called cash tokens, which is reuse of tokens.
cues.zh: 接著是快取 Token，也就是重複利用的 Token。

cues.en: Because whenever we begin to do conversations, we will ask a question and then we'll do a follow-up.
cues.zh: 因為開始進行多輪對話後，會先問一個問題，然後接著追問。

cues.en: And we don't need to spend tokens on the first part of the question again, because that would be the same answer.
cues.zh: 前面相同的內容，就不需要再以完整計算成本處理一次。

cues.en: It only happens when you begin to use more tokens, like 1024.
cues.zh: 通常要累積較多 Token 才會開始快取，例如 1,024 個。

cues.en: Before that, it will not try to cash tokens.
cues.zh: 少於這個數量時，通常不會嘗試快取。

cues.en: But if you have some heavy use and with very much follow-up, all your things will probably be cash tokens, and cash tokens are cheaper in general.
cues.zh: 如果使用量大，又有很多追問，大部分重複內容就可能成為快取 Token；一般而言，快取 Token 比較便宜。

cues.en: Finally, we have the output tokens, which can be put into two categories.
cues.zh: 最後是輸出 Token，可以分成兩類。

cues.en: The first being what we get back.
cues.zh: 第一類就是實際收到的回答。

cues.en: So when we ask, what is the capital of France?
cues.zh: 例如問「法國的首都是哪裡？」，

cues.en: We will get that it's Paris.
cues.zh: 得到的答案是巴黎，

cues.en: And we pay for the word that the capital is Paris.
cues.zh: 就要支付「法國的首都是巴黎」這段文字的 Token 費用。

cues.en: If we use reasoning models, like Chat-GPT-5, we are also getting some tokens that are being
cues.zh: 如果使用 GPT-5 等推理模型，還會有一些 Token，

cues.en: used for the internal reasoning of the model.
cues.zh: 用來進行模型內部的推理。

cues.en: So it might think about what is the capital of France before it answers.
cues.zh: 例如回答前，先思考法國的首都到底是哪裡。

cues.en: Or if it's a very complex question, it will talk back and forward with itself and use those.
cues.zh: 如果問題很複雜，它可能反覆自問自答，也會消耗 Token。

cues.en: You don't really get those tokens back, but you still pay for them, because they are still tokens being used by the LLM.
cues.zh: 這些 Token 不會實際回傳給你，但仍要付費，因為 LLM 確實使用了它們。

cues.en: These are called reasoning tokens, and they will be part of the output token.
cues.zh: 這些稱為推理 Token，屬於輸出 Token 的一部分。

cues.en: So you will see an output token, for example, of 1000 output tokens, and then you will know 300 of them were used for reasoning, while the last 700 was actually the
cues.zh: 例如顯示總共用了 1,000 個輸出 Token，其中 300 個用於推理，剩下 700 個才是

cues.en: text you received back.
cues.zh: 你真正收到的文字。

cues.en: Let's see some examples, and also why this can be very difficult to understand, and you need to learn from experience how tokens work.
cues.zh: 來看看幾個範例，也看看為什麼這件事不容易理解，需要透過經驗掌握 Token 的運作方式。

cues.en: So this is one of the examples in the sample repo, so you can go check out the code if you want to.
cues.zh: 這是範例儲存庫裡的一個範例，想看的話可以自行查看程式碼。

cues.en: But if we take a simple setup like our Hello World, and just ask a question,
cues.zh: 採用和 Hello World 類似的簡單設定，只問一個問題，

cues.en: what is the capital of France, we get the output, of course, that the capital of France is Paris.
cues.zh: 也就是「法國的首都是哪裡？」，自然會得到「法國的首都是巴黎」。

cues.en: And if we go to the sample repo,
cues.zh: 如果進入範例儲存庫，

cues.en: which we have here, we can go in and see that I'm just using the chat
cues.zh: 也就是這裡，可以看到我只使用 ChatClient，

cues.en: client, and then I'm taking out from the response, which is where we have our text back, the capital of France, we can also
cues.zh: 再從回應裡取出文字，也就是法國首都的答案。此外，還能

cues.en: get a usage object.
cues.zh: 取得 Usage 物件。

cues.en: And if that usage object is different from zero, meaning the LLM we are working with support reporting usage back, and most of them
cues.zh: 只要 Usage 不是空值，就表示目前使用的 LLM 支援回報用量，而現在多數模型

cues.en: do now, we get our input tokens, we get our cache tokens, we get our reasoning tokens, and how many of them were output
cues.zh: 都支援。裡面有輸入 Token、快取 Token、推理 Token，以及輸出

cues.en: tokens, and how many of them were reasoning.
cues.zh: Token 數量，和其中用於推理的數量。

cues.en: So that is what we are seeing here.
cues.zh: 這就是目前畫面顯示的資訊。

cues.en: We are not doing anything special yet.
cues.zh: 我們還沒有做任何特別的操作。

cues.en: But some interesting thing happens, because we are using here a chat-gpt 4.1 nano, one of the cheapest models you can get.
cues.zh: 不過有些有趣的現象。這裡使用 gpt-4.1-nano，是能找到的最便宜模型之一。

cues.en: And it's used some input tokens.
cues.zh: 它使用了一些輸入 Token。

cues.en: What is the capital of France?
cues.zh: 提示詞是「法國的首都是哪裡？」。

cues.en: There's no extra tools or anything.
cues.zh: 沒有額外的工具或其他內容。

cues.en: So this is the raw.
cues.zh: 所以這是最單純的情況。

cues.en: What is the capital of France is 14 tokens.
cues.zh: 這句問題用了 14 個 Token。

cues.en: It used zero cache tokens, because it's a too little sentence to begin to cache, and there's no follow-up.
cues.zh: 快取 Token 是零，因為句子太短，不會開始快取，而且也沒有追問。

cues.en: And it used eight tokens for the output.
cues.zh: 輸出則用了 8 個 Token，

cues.en: The capital of France is Paris.
cues.zh: 也就是「法國的首都是巴黎」。

cues.en: And zero of them was reasoning, because it's not a reasoning model.
cues.zh: 推理 Token 是零，因為它不是推理模型。

cues.en: It spent roughly one second doing this.
cues.zh: 完成這次請求，大約花了一秒。

cues.en: In general, you will see that Azure is faster at answering back than OpenAI is.
cues.zh: 一般來說，Azure 回應通常會比 OpenAI 快一些。

cues.en: But it's all depending on what time of day you do it.
cues.zh: 但這也取決於你在一天中的哪個時段使用。

cues.en: If you do it in peak hours, it will be longer.
cues.zh: 尖峰時間可能比較久，

cues.en: If you do it in non-peak hours, it will be shorter.
cues.zh: 離峰時間可能比較快。

cues.en: So you can't really look at the time and say, okay, every time I will ask, what is the capital of France?
cues.zh: 所以不能只看這個時間，就以為每次問「法國的首都是哪裡？」

cues.en: It will be like this.
cues.zh: 都一定花相同的時間。

cues.en: Sometimes it will be longer.
cues.zh: 有時會比較久，

cues.en: Sometimes it will be shorter.
cues.zh: 有時會比較快。

cues.en: But I did it with different models at the exact same time, so they can roughly be compared.
cues.zh: 不過我是在相同時間測試不同模型，所以大致上還可以比較。

cues.en: We also have the same code, but now with another model, GPT 5 nano.
cues.zh: 同一段程式，也換成另一個模型 gpt-5-nano 試試。

cues.en: So we get, in this case, it actually used one token less.
cues.zh: 這次輸入竟然少用了一個 Token。

cues.en: It must have figured out that it wanted to do it in a different way.
cues.zh: 它可能選擇以不同方式處理。

cues.en: It shouldn't really happen, but that's the way it is.
cues.zh: 理論上不應有這種差異，但結果就是如此。

cues.en: We see that it gives a shorter output, but it used more output tokens, and it's also using slightly more time.
cues.zh: 可以看到，回答文字比較短，輸出 Token 卻更多，花的時間也稍長。

cues.en: And the reason for that, we can see, is it's using more reasoning tokens.
cues.zh: 從這裡可以看出原因：它使用了更多推理 Token。

cues.en: And this is because GPT 5 nano is a very, very, I won't call it unintelligent,
cues.zh: 這是因為 gpt-5-nano 的能力相對有限；我不會說它不聰明，

cues.en: but not the most intelligent of these models.
cues.zh: 但它不是這些模型裡最聰明的。

cues.en: So it needs to think, oh, this can be a serious question.
cues.zh: 所以它得先思考：「這可能是一個需要認真處理的問題。」

cues.en: I need to think how to give that answer.
cues.zh: 「我得想想該怎麼回答。」

cues.en: So it actually spent some tokens on this.
cues.zh: 因此就花了一些 Token 在推理上。

cues.en: So in this case, using this one over here, despite it actually having a higher per cost token count, will cost less.
cues.zh: 所以在這種情況下，前面這個模型即使每個 Token 單價較高，總費用反而比較低。

cues.en: And we can also see we get slightly faster back.
cues.zh: 而且回應速度也稍微快一點。

cues.en: But then something interesting happened.
cues.zh: 接著又出現一個有趣的現象。

cues.en: If I go to the biggest and greatest model, GPT 5.2, as of this recording,
cues.zh: 如果改用錄製當下規模最大、能力最強的 GPT-5.2，

cues.en: we get exactly the same input, exactly the same output.
cues.zh: 輸入完全相同，輸出文字也完全相同。

cues.en: And then we see that our output token is only six tokens here, despite it being the model that can think for a long time.
cues.zh: 但這次只用了 6 個輸出 Token，雖然這是一個能長時間思考的模型。

cues.en: This is because GPT 5.2, we could also have taken GPT 5, is a more intelligent model, so it knows that this question
cues.zh: 這是因為 GPT-5.2 更聰明，換 GPT-5 也類似。它知道這個問題

cues.en: is not a hard question.
cues.zh: 並不困難，

cues.en: So it doesn't need to think about it.
cues.zh: 所以不需要特別思考。

cues.en: This model has less world knowledge.
cues.zh: 這個小模型知道的世界知識比較少，

cues.en: This one has more world knowledge.
cues.zh: 這個大模型的世界知識比較多。

cues.en: So this was just ready to answer question back, while here it needed to think about where it had that in its storage.
cues.zh: 因此，大模型直接就能回答；小模型則需要想想知識存放在哪裡。

cues.en: So for that reason, you cannot really just say, bigger model, more cost, in terms of output, because things like this.
cues.zh: 所以不能直接斷言模型越大，輸出費用就一定越高，因為可能出現這種情況。

cues.en: But have you asked a very scientific question about some universal models and so on?
cues.zh: 但如果問的是非常科學性的問題，例如宇宙模型等等，

cues.en: This model would have definitely began to use a lot of reasoning tokens and way more reasoning tokens than this one over here.
cues.zh: 大模型肯定會開始大量推理，消耗的推理 Token 也會比這個小模型多很多。

cues.en: We will talk about reasoning in general and how much reasoning and so on.
cues.zh: 後面會再談推理，以及推理強度等設定。

cues.en: But just to show you, it is very, very difficult to figure out.
cues.zh: 這裡只是要讓你知道，確實很難一概而論。

cues.en: So here we actually use the biggest models and spend the least amount of tokens.
cues.zh: 這次反而是最大的模型，用了最少的 Token。

cues.en: Those tokens still cost more, which we will see in one second.
cues.zh: 不過這些 Token 的單價仍比較高，等等就會看到。

cues.en: But it is a balancing act on how cheap or how intelligent you need to have
cues.zh: 所以需要在費用和所需的模型智慧程度之間，

cues.en: a model.
cues.zh: 取得平衡。

cues.en: This is a simple question.
cues.zh: 這只是一個簡單問題，

cues.en: So we should definitely use a simple model.
cues.zh: 因此應該使用簡單的模型。

cues.en: In this case, I would use this one over here, despite this being slightly less tokens.
cues.zh: 在這個例子，我會選這個便宜模型，即使另一個模型少用了一點 Token。

cues.en: While here, it is kind of overkill because you think, oh, this is a serious question.
cues.zh: 中間這個模型反而有點用力過度，好像認為這是個非常嚴肅的問題，

cues.en: We need to think a lot about it.
cues.zh: 得花很多心力思考，

cues.en: So that wouldn't fit well.
cues.zh: 所以不太適合。

cues.en: While in the bigger models, this is way overkill for a question like the capital of France.
cues.zh: 至於更大的模型，用來回答法國首都這種問題又大材小用了。

cues.en: It shows that by being good at answering it.
cues.zh: 它確實答得很好，顯示自己的能力，

cues.en: But still, why spend the tokens for a higher price?
cues.zh: 但為什麼要花更高的 Token 單價呢？

cues.en: Because this is like 50 times more priced than this one is.
cues.zh: 因為它的價格大約是這個模型的 50 倍。

cues.en: But let's talk price.
cues.zh: 接著來談實際價格。
